title: Overdue invoice query loses its tenant filter and gains a query per row

consumerGuidance.architecture: EF Core against SQL Server. Every tenant-scoped query must filter on ITenantContext.TenantId; there is no global query filter configured on AppDbContext.
consumerGuidance.notes: OverdueInvoiceQuery is reached from the tenant-facing /reports/overdue endpoint and from the new internal admin endpoint. Supplied CI timing shows the endpoint's p95 rising from 180 ms to 9.4 s on the seeded 12,000-invoice dataset.

mustCite: the removed TenantId predicate and that no global query filter exists on AppDbContext
the tenant-facing /reports/overdue caller that still reaches this method
the consequence that one tenant's report now returns every tenant's overdue invoices
a correction that keeps the tenant predicate for tenant callers and gives the admin path its own deliberate query
the per-row customer lookup inside the foreach and the unbounded ToListAsync that feeds it
the supplied timing evidence showing p95 rising from 180 ms to 9.4 s on 12,000 invoices
the consequence of one query per invoice against SQL Server on a request path
a correction such as projecting the customer name in the original query or batching the lookups

forbiddenFindings.example: Requiring compiled queries, AsSplitQuery or a caching layer with no supplied measurement showing they matter.
Requiring CQRS read models or a reporting database for this endpoint.
Objecting to query syntax versus method syntax.

notes: The cross-tenant exposure is the safety finding and stays explicit even though CI passes. The cost finding is admissible because the case supplies a measurement.
